title: The realised capacity tracker keeps each day's LOWEST window, so the billed peak and the capacity line are understated
claim: tariff._one_per_day keeps an entry when kw < best[day], so under distinct_days (the default) PeakTracker records each day's smallest closed window and billed_peak_kw reads 1.93 kW against 4.06 kW for three days of the winter_extreme capacity-tariff plan; 0.47-2.13 kW low on all 8 price shapes.
mechanism: tariff.py:491 `elif day not in best or kw < best[day][0]` (docstring: 'Each dated day's highest entry'). _close_window folds every closed window through it, so a day's recorded peak walks down to its quietest window; billed_peak_kw (ledger capacity line via book_capacity, the published billed peak) and threshold_kw (the plan's capacity threshold) both read the understated list.

evidence.contention_note: fan-out: up to three seats share the box; a count, contention-immune

metric_definition: tracker_peak_err = |PeakTracker.billed_peak_kw - mean of the 3 highest per-day window maxima| after 3 days of the plan's house power (distinct_days on, 60-min windows)
phenomenon_property: Under a distinct-days tariff each day contributes its highest metering window, and the billed peak is the mean of the k highest such days.

null_control.note: booking the same billed peak twice books it once (book_capacity sets): the line restates whatever the tracker says, so the error is the tracker's alone

proposed_fix_scope: tariff._one_per_day: keep the larger kw per day
